drills.title: 1v1 defending in a channel
drills.summary: Close down an attacker, slow them, steer them away from the line and win the ball.
drills.setup: A channel 8 m wide and 15 m long. The defender starts on one end line with the ball, the attacker on the far end line. A server stands behind the defender's line with spare balls.
instructions: The defender passes to the attacker and closes them down.
The attacker scores by dribbling over the defender's end line.
The defender scores by winning the ball and passing it to the server.
Swap roles after each turn; first to five points.
coaching_points: Close down quickly while the ball travels, then slow down with short steps as you arrive.
Arrive side-on, about an arm's length away, on your toes.
Show the attacker towards the touchline or their weaker foot, away from the line they want.
Be patient: tackle when the ball leaves their feet, not while they have it under control.

variations.title: Attacker at jogging pace
variations.change: The attacker may only dribble at jogging pace in a 6 m wide channel, so the defender can practise the approach.
instructions: The defender passes and closes down; the attacker dribbles at jogging pace and may not speed up.
The defender practises slowing down, getting side-on and showing the attacker one way.
Tackle only when the ball leaves the attacker's feet; pass it to the server to score.
Swap roles after each turn.

variations.title: Pass and press
variations.change: Live 1v1 in an 8 m channel: the defender passes, then presses.

variations.title: Wider channel, longer approach
variations.change: A 12 m wide, 20 m long channel: more space to defend and a longer run to judge.
variations.setup: A channel 12 m wide and 20 m long. The defender starts on one end line with the ball, the attacker on the far end line. A server stands behind the defender's line with spare balls.
coaching_points: Curve your run so you arrive already showing the attacker one way.
The longer the run, the earlier you must start slowing down.
With more space, delay: stay goal-side and wait for help or a heavy touch.
Tackle when the ball leaves their feet, not before.

variations.title: Recover and stop
variations.change: The defender starts beside the attacker, not in front, and must recover goal-side before defending.
variations.setup: A channel 8 m wide and 15 m long. The attacker and defender start side by side, 3 m apart, at one end; the server stands behind them with the balls.
instructions: The server passes to the attacker; both players go as the pass is played.
The attacker scores by dribbling over the far end line.
The defender recovers goal-side, then delays and wins the ball; passing it back to the server scores.
Swap roles after each turn.
coaching_points: Sprint back on the shortest line to get between the attacker and the line.
Once goal-side, slow down, get side-on and show them away from the line.
Don't tackle from the side or behind: a miss or a foul gives them a free run.

media.caption: Pass, press, slow down and steer the attacker wide

steps.label: The defender passes to the attacker and closes down while the ball travels
Slow down with short steps and arrive side-on, showing the attacker to the left
The attacker is pushed towards the touchline; the defender stays goal-side and matches the speed
A heavy touch: the defender steps in and wins the ball
Pass to the server to score

media.caption: Harder: recover goal-side first, then stop the attacker

steps.label: The server passes to the attacker; both go
The attacker drives at the line; the defender sprints on the shortest line to get goal-side
Goal-side: slow down, get side-on and show the attacker towards the touchline
The attacker tries to cut inside; the defender wins the ball
Pass back to the server to score

drills.title: Receive and shoot past a goalkeeper
drills.summary: Receive a pass, set the ball with one touch and finish past a goalkeeper, in small groups at several goals.
drills.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. A server stands 16 m out with the balls; a cone 10 m out marks where shooters receive. No more than three shooters per goal: use more goals for bigger groups.
instructions: The server passes into the shooter's path towards the cone.
The shooter takes one touch to set the ball, then shoots before the goalkeeper is set.
The shooter collects the ball and becomes the server; the server joins the shooters.
coaching_points: Look at the goal and the goalkeeper before the ball arrives.
Open your body so the first touch sets the ball out of your feet towards goal.
Laces for power, side-foot for placement; keep your head over the ball to keep it low.
Follow your shot in for a rebound.

variations.title: Shoot a still ball
variations.change: Shoot a still ball from 8 m; any technique, toe pokes and laces welcome.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper and a row of balls 8 m out. No more than three shooters per goal.
instructions: Shooters take turns striking a still ball at goal.
Aim for the corners, away from the goalkeeper.
Collect your ball and go again.
coaching_points: Plant your standing foot beside the ball.
Toe poke or laces: strike through the middle of the ball.
Keep your head still and watch the ball as you strike it.

variations.title: Receive, set and shoot
variations.change: The server passes into the shooter's path; one touch to set, then shoot.

variations.title: First time from a pass across
variations.change: The server plays the ball across from the side; finish first time where you can, low and across the goalkeeper.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper. A server stands at the side of the box, level with the penalty spot; shooters start 16 m out. No more than three shooters per goal.
instructions: The server plays the ball across the box.
The shooter times the run to meet it and finishes first time, or with one touch if the ball is awkward.
Swap the server's side every five balls.
coaching_points: Adjust your feet early to the line of the ball.
Side-foot through the ball for accuracy when finishing first time.
Low and across the goalkeeper: a save is harder to hold and may spill to a teammate.

variations.title: 1v1 against a defender
variations.change: A defender passes out and presses; the attacker may only shoot once past the cone line 12 m out.
variations.setup: A goal with a goalkeeper and a cone line 12 m out. The defender starts beside the goal with the balls, the attacker 20 m out.
instructions: The defender passes to the attacker, then presses.
The attacker must get past the cone line before shooting.
The defender scores by winning the ball and dribbling it out past the attacker's start.
Swap roles after each turn.
coaching_points: Attack the defender at speed, then shift the ball past them into the shooting zone.
Shoot early once you are past: the defender is recovering.
Low and across the goalkeeper.

media.caption: Receive in stride, set with one touch, shoot low

steps.label: The server passes into the shooter's path; the shooter runs onto it
One touch sets the ball out of the feet towards goal
Shoot low into the corner before the goalkeeper is set

media.caption: Easier: strike a still ball

steps.label: Plant beside the ball and strike low towards a corner

media.caption: Harder: meet a pass across and finish first time

steps.label: The server plays it across; the shooter times the run to meet it
First-time finish, low and across the goalkeeper

media.caption: Hardest: beat the defender, then finish

steps.label: The defender passes out to the attacker and presses
The attacker drives at the defender and shifts the ball past them
Into the shooting zone past the cone line
Shoot early, low and across the goalkeeper

media.caption: Source: England Football – How to design a football shooting session
Source: England Football – Finishing session: techniques to score (1v1 finishing)

drills.title: Check away and show to receive
drills.summary: Move away from a defender to make space, then come back into it at an angle to receive.
drills.setup: A channel 10 m wide and 20 m long. A server with balls at one end; the receiver in the middle with a defender on the far side of them.
instructions: The receiver checks away from the server, taking the defender with them.
Then they show sharply back towards the server at an angle, into the space they made.
The server passes; the receiver takes it on the half-turn and passes back.
The defender follows but does not tackle. Swap roles after five receptions.
coaching_points: Look where the defender is before you move.
Go away first to make the space, then come back into it with a sharp change of speed and direction.
Show at an angle, not straight at the server, so you can see the defender and the field.
Arrive as the pass is played, and ask for it.
Open your body and receive with the foot furthest from the defender.

variations.title: Check away from a cone
variations.change: A cone stands in for the defender, so the receiver can practise the timing of the double movement.
variations.setup: A channel 10 m wide and 20 m long. A server with balls at one end; a cone in the middle stands in for the defender.
instructions: The receiver jogs away from the server past the cone.
Then they sprint back at an angle to show for the ball.
The server passes; receive and pass back.
Swap after five receptions.

variations.title: Show against a shadow defender
variations.change: A defender follows the receiver but does not tackle.

variations.title: Live defender, set it back
variations.change: The defender competes and may intercept; the receiver must get free and set the ball back to the server.
instructions: The receiver checks away and shows to get free of the defender.
The server passes only when the receiver is free.
The receiver sets the ball back first time or with two touches; the defender scores by intercepting.
Swap roles after five attempts.

variations.title: Live defender, turn and play forward
variations.change: A target player stands at the far end: if the defender is not tight, turn and pass to the target.
variations.setup: A channel 10 m wide and 20 m long. A server with balls at one end and a target player at the other; the receiver in the middle with a live defender.
instructions: The receiver checks away and shows to get free.
If the defender is tight, set the ball back to the server; if not, turn and pass to the target.
A pass to the target scores two, a set-back one; the defender scores by intercepting.
Swap roles after five attempts.
coaching_points: Check over your shoulder before the ball arrives: is the defender tight or off?
If there is space, turn on your first touch, away from the defender.
If they are tight, set it back and move again.

media.caption: Check away to make space, then show at an angle

steps.label: The receiver checks away, taking the defender towards the far end
Then shows sharply back at an angle, into the space made
The server passes; receive on the half-turn with the foot furthest from the defender
Pass back and go again

media.caption: Easier: a cone stands in for the defender

steps.label: Jog away past the cone
Sprint back at an angle to show for the ball
Receive on the half-turn
Pass back and go again

media.caption: Hardest: the defender is not tight, so turn and play forward

steps.label: Check away, taking the defender with you
Show at an angle; the defender is slow to follow
Receive side-on and check: the defender is off
Turn away from the defender on the first touch
Play forward to the target

drills.title: 4v2 pressing in pairs
drills.summary: Two players press together: one closes the ball, the other covers the next pass, to win the ball back.
drills.setup: A 15 by 15 m square. Six players in three pairs, each in its own bib colour: two pairs keep the ball, one pair presses.
instructions: The two pairs keep the ball; six passes in a row scores a point.
The pressing pair works together to win the ball or force it out; a win scores them a point.
When the pressers win it or the ball goes out, the pair that lost it presses next.
coaching_points: The player nearest the ball presses first; the partner covers the pass they are most likely to try.
Approach side-on and curve your run to cut off one passing lane as you close.
Get within arm's reach: close enough that the passer has to rush.
Press together on a trigger: a heavy touch, a backward pass, or a player facing away from play.
Force play towards a corner or a side: the line is an extra defender.

variations.title: 3v2 in a small square
variations.change: Three players keep the ball in a 10 by 10 m square, so the pair has fewer passes to cover.
variations.setup: A 10 by 10 m square. Three players keep the ball against a pressing pair.
instructions: The three keep the ball; four passes in a row scores a point.
The pair presses together to win it; a win scores them a point.
Rotate so everyone presses for 60 seconds.

variations.title: 4v2 in pairs
variations.change: Two pairs keep the ball in a 15 by 15 m square against a pressing pair.

variations.title: Bigger square
variations.change: A 20 by 20 m square: more ground to cover, so the cover player's position matters more.
variations.setup: A 20 by 20 m square. Six players in three pairs, each in its own bib colour: two pairs keep the ball, one pair presses.

variations.title: 4v4 to mini-goals
variations.change: Two teams of four play to two mini-goals each; the team without the ball presses as a unit.
variations.setup: A 20 by 25 m pitch with a halfway line and two mini-goals at each end. Two teams of four, each in a 3-1 shape: three defenders and one striker.
instructions: Each team attacks two mini-goals and defends two.
In possession, the three stay in their own half and the striker stays behind the other team's defenders; score from your own half or through the striker.
Without the ball, all four may press anywhere.
A coach plays a new ball in after each goal or when the ball goes out.
coaching_points: The nearest player presses; the others move together to cover and stay balanced around the ball.
Keep the middle compact and force play wide.
Watch the striker behind you: don't all chase the ball and leave them free.
Lose the ball? Switch to defending straight away.

media.caption: The nearest presses, the partner covers, and the pass back is the trigger

steps.label: A1 passes to A2. P2, the nearest, closes on a curved run that blocks the pass up to A3; P1 covers the pass across
Blocked, A2 plays back to A1. The backward pass is the trigger: P1 jumps onto A1 while P2 cuts off the return
A1 is trapped against the line with both passes blocked; the pair win the ball

media.caption: Easier: 3v2 in a small square

steps.label: A1 passes to A2; P2 closes on a curved run that blocks the pass across to A3
P1 covers the pass back, so A2 has to dribble towards the corner
Trapped in the corner: P2 wins the ball

media.caption: Hardest: 4v4, the team without the ball presses as a unit

steps.label: Blues circulate: A2 to A3. The nearest orange, B1, presses on a curved run that blocks the pass inside; B3 drops to cover the striker
With the inside closed, A3 goes down the line; B1 traps them against the touchline
B1 wins the ball; orange striker B4 is free behind the blues
Quick pass to B4 before the blues recover
B4 scores in the mini-goal

media.caption: Source: FIFA Training Centre – Preventing progression through central areas (4v2 and 4v4 pressing games)

drills.title: 4v3 transition game
drills.summary: Attack a goal 4v3; when the ball is lost, win it back at once, and when it's won, break out fast.
drills.setup: A 20 by 20 m area in front of a goal with a goalkeeper. Four attackers and three defenders inside it; a server with the balls stands on the far end line.
instructions: The server passes to an attacker; the four attackers try to score: one point.
The defenders try to win the ball and dribble it over the far end line: two points.
If the attackers lose the ball, they press at once to win it back before it crosses the line.
Restart from the server after a goal, a save, or the ball going out. Swap roles every three minutes.
coaching_points: Attacking: use the extra player, so someone is always free in space.
Lose it? The nearest player presses straight away; the others cut off the forward passes.
Win it? Look forward, play forward and run forward, quickly, before the attackers recover.
Defending the goal: stay compact and make the attackers play around you, not through you.

variations.title: 4v2
variations.change: Only two defenders, so the attackers keep the ball more and transitions are easier to read.
variations.setup: A 20 by 20 m area in front of a goal with a goalkeeper. Four attackers and two defenders inside it; a server with the balls stands on the far end line.

variations.title: 4v3
variations.change: Four attackers against three defenders; winning the ball means a break for the far line.

variations.title: Five-second rule
variations.change: Defenders who win the ball must cross the line within 5 seconds; attackers score a point if they win it back within 5 seconds.
instructions: The server passes to an attacker; the four attackers try to score: one point.
Defenders who win the ball have 5 seconds to dribble it over the far end line: two points.
Attackers who win the ball back within 5 seconds of losing it score a point, and keep attacking.
Restart from the server after a goal, a save, or the ball going out. Swap roles every three minutes.

variations.title: Counter into mini-goals
variations.change: Defenders who win the ball counter into two mini-goals on the far line within 5 seconds; attackers who win it back can shoot at once.
variations.setup: A 20 by 20 m area in front of a goal with a goalkeeper, and two mini-goals on the far end line. Four attackers and three defenders inside it; a server with the balls stands between the mini-goals.
instructions: The server passes to an attacker; the four attackers try to score: one point.
Defenders who win the ball have 5 seconds to score in either mini-goal: two points.
Attackers who win the ball back can shoot at once.
Restart from the server after each goal, save or ball out. Swap roles every three minutes.

media.caption: Ball lost: the nearest attacker presses at once; ball won: break out fast

steps.label: The server passes in to A1; the attackers spread out so one is always free
A1 tries to pass through to A4; B2 steps in and intercepts
Transition: A2, the nearest attacker, presses B2 at once
B2 escapes the press and plays forward to B1 in space
B1 dribbles over the line: two points

media.caption: Easier: 4v2

steps.label: The server passes in to A1; the attackers spread out
A1 tries to pass through to A4; B2 intercepts
Transition: A2 presses B2 at once, and A1 cuts off the pass to B1
Pressed from two sides, B2 loses it back to A2

media.caption: Hardest: win it and counter into a mini-goal within 5 seconds

steps.label: The server passes in to A1; the attackers spread out
A1 tries to pass through to A4; B2 intercepts
Five seconds to score: B2 drives at the mini-goal while A2 counter-presses
Shot into the mini-goal before the press arrives

drills.title: Goalkeeper rolls and throws to targets
drills.summary: Catch a served ball, then roll or throw it accurately to targets at different distances.
drills.setup: A goal with the goalkeeper. A server 10 m out with the balls. Two mini-goals as targets: one 15 m away to the left, one 22 m away to the right.
instructions: The server throws or volleys the ball at the goalkeeper, who catches it.
The server calls a target: roll to the near one, or javelin throw to the far one.
Ten catches, mixing the targets; count how many reach them.
coaching_points: Every distribution is a pass: weight it so a teammate could take it in their stride.
Roll: step towards the target, bend low, and let go just before your hand passes your front foot, so the ball doesn't bounce.
Follow through in a straight line at the target.
Javelin throw: side-on, bring the arm round at shoulder height and push the ball flat at the target.

variations.title: Roll through a gate
variations.change: No catch first: the goalkeeper rolls the ball through a 2 m gate 10 m away.
variations.setup: Balls beside the goalkeeper and a 2 m wide gate of cones 10 m away.
instructions: Roll the ball through the gate.
Ten rolls, then move the gate further away or make it narrower.
coaching_points: Step towards the gate with the opposite foot to your rolling hand.
Bend low and let go just before your hand passes your front foot.
Follow through in a straight line at the gate.

variations.title: Catch, then roll or javelin
variations.change: Catch a served ball, then roll or javelin throw to one of two targets.

variations.title: Overarm throw to a far target
variations.change: A third target 25 m away for an overarm throw; the server calls short, medium or long.
variations.setup: A goal with the goalkeeper. A server 10 m out with the balls. Three mini-goals as targets: 15 m to the left, 22 m to the right and 25 m straight out.
instructions: The server throws or volleys the ball at the goalkeeper, who catches it.
The server calls short, medium or long: roll, javelin or overarm throw.
Ten catches, mixing the calls; count how many reach their target.
coaching_points: Overarm: side-on, ball held back with a straight arm, step forward and bring the arm over the top.
Release a little in front of your head so the ball travels flat, not high.
Choose the throw by distance: roll short, javelin medium, overarm long.

variations.title: Throw to a moving teammate
variations.change: A teammate moves between the targets and calls; the goalkeeper picks the throw and puts it into their stride.
variations.setup: A goal with the goalkeeper. A server 10 m out with the balls, and a teammate moving around 15 to 25 m away.
instructions: The server throws or volleys the ball at the goalkeeper, who catches it.
The teammate moves into space and calls for the ball.
The goalkeeper picks the throw for the distance and plays it into the teammate's path.
Ten catches; the teammate scores each throw they can take in their stride.
coaching_points: Look up as you catch: where is the teammate going, not just where they are?
Throw into the space ahead of them, not at their feet.
Distribute quickly, before an opponent could recover.

media.caption: Catch, then roll to the near target

steps.label: The server volleys at the goalkeeper: step in and catch
The server calls 'near': step towards it, bend low and roll it in

media.caption: Easier: roll through a gate

steps.label: Step towards the gate, bend low and roll it through

media.caption: Harder: overarm to the far target

steps.label: The server volleys at the goalkeeper: step in and catch
The call is 'long': overarm throw to the far target

media.caption: Hardest: read the teammate's run and throw into their stride

steps.label: The server volleys at the goalkeeper: catch it
Look up: the teammate is running into space on the right and calling
Javelin throw into the space ahead of them
